name: Stormwall
description: A young supergiant barely twenty million years old, already dying in fast-forward. Its wind sculpts the two giants' atmospheres into streaming tails. The whole system has an expiry date astronomers state to three significant figures.

stars.name: Stormwall Giant
stars.description: A bloated blue-white supergiant shedding mass in great slow gusts. Its photosphere could swallow the inner orbits whole. Every model agrees it will detonate within the million years.

planets.name: Windbreak
planets.description: A banded giant with its atmosphere streaming away under the supergiant's gale. Cloud decks tear and reform on weekly cycles. Probes measure mass loss directly, watching a world evaporate.

planets.name: Leeward
planets.description: A second giant sheltered slightly by its sibling's bulk, keeping two icy moons. Tidal kneading warms the inner moon's buried sea. Evacuation plans exist for when the primary goes.

moons.name: Stay
moons.description: An ice moon with a tidally warmed ocean, the system's best bet for native life. Cryovolcanoes dot the south pole in long chains. Its habitability has a hard deadline nobody names.

moons.name: Execution
moons.description: A dark cratered rock that will witness the end from the front row. Seismometers record the star's growing instability. Its name was voted on by the evacuation crews.

comets.name: Brief Glory
comets.description: A short-period comet vaporizing a little more with every pass of the fierce primary. Its tail stretches a full astronomical unit at perihelion. Astronomers log its decay like a terminal chart.
